inputs.original_text: South Portland’s schools are preparing to cut more than 70 positions, and families deserve a plain accounting—not another round of excuses. A school system’s first duty is to educate children and support the people who teach them, not protect administrative priorities. Taxpayers have a right to know how this happened and who is accountable. Careful stewardship, clear priorities, and respect for families should come before bureaucratic comfort.
inputs.modified_text: South Portland’s schools are preparing to cut more than 70 positions, and families and taxpayers deserve straight answers. When a system claims it must reduce the people who educate and support children, the public should ask whether its priorities have been right. Schools exist to serve students and families—not to shield bureaucracy from scrutiny. Those responsible owe the community a clear accounting and real accountability.
